body: Maybe prefer `jest.fn`. We should avoid to add new code with `sinon`. We probably remove it at some point.

You should probably use `done` for finish the test. I think the assertions inside `setImmediate` are executed after the test, if they fail all the process will fail instead of just the test case.

You can ensure how many assertions you expect in an async test with:

```js
expect.assertions(numberOfAssertionsExpected);
```
Maybe cast the value with `Boolean()`, it will ensure that the value will be a `boolean`. With the actual condition the value can be anything thruthy or a `boolean`.

Actually we can't because the method don't return the promise.

But you can still use await Promise.resolve() to force the event loop to run the render function. That's what setImmediate does here.

Was just a small comment if it's feasible it might be easier to read than setImmediate (and safer)

After looking at some jest issues, it seems that it handles returned promises and since my main issue with setImmediate is that when the test fail jest breaks, I ended up creating a new promise and in the then do my tests. It's not as smart but `¯\_(ツ)_/¯`
You could use the shorthand method: `.not.toHaveBeenCalled()`
You could use the shorthand method: `.toHaveBeenCalled()`
You could use the shorthand method: `.toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)`
You could use the shorthand method: `.toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(expect.any(Object), true)`
I've switched to the number of call counts because it give a finer grain when there is a fail. In this case it would not matter much, but I still prefer consistency of API usage. Is that ok?
